items.t: EU summit fails to agree budget and €45bn Ukraine loan
items.d: Leaders broke up without a deal on the 2028-34 budget; Czechia, Hungary and Slovakia held out on the Ukraine loan. Talks resume on 17-18 December.

items.t: Ukraine offers Black Sea ceasefire to protect grain exports
items.d: Kyiv has submitted a Black Sea truce proposal and awaits Moscow's reply, after Russia reportedly hit two foreign grain ships near Odesa.

items.t: Oil near multi-month highs as Gulf conflict threatens supply
items.d: Brent traded around $96 a barrel amid reports of tanker incidents and mines near Hormuz, feeding fears of higher fuel and energy bills.

items.t: Spain votes on Sunday after final campaign appeals
items.d: Pedro Sánchez and his rivals made last pitches to voters ahead of Sunday's general election, with cost of living a key issue.

items.t: New Zealand coalition one seat short of majority
items.d: Official results give the governing coalition 65 of 130 seats, leaving it reliant on talks with smaller parties to govern.

items.t: Canada's top court upholds Quebec religious-symbols law
items.d: In a 6-1 ruling the Supreme Court largely upheld Bill 21, which bars some public workers from wearing religious symbols.

items.t: Wall Street rebounds, Nasdaq up over 2%
items.d: US stocks bounced sharply in a volatile week for AI shares, while the 10-year Treasury yield climbed towards 4.94%.

items.t: Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy over fuel costs
items.d: The Norwegian low-cost transatlantic airline blamed soaring jet fuel prices, a sign of how the energy shock is hitting travel.

items.t: Study questions Amazon's Black Friday 'deals'
items.d: An analysis found about two-thirds of sale items cost the same or less in earlier months; Amazon disputes the findings.

items.t: SAP weighs over 10,000 job cuts in AI overhaul
items.d: Europe's biggest software firm is reportedly considering deep cuts as it restructures around AI.

items.t: OpenAI countersues Apple over trade secrets and suppliers
items.d: OpenAI says Apple pressured shared suppliers to shun its devices and misused hardware designs, escalating a fight Apple began in July.

items.t: SAP confirms cyberattack; source code reportedly hit
items.d: Hackers reportedly used stolen staff tokens to copy and alter code on GitHub. SAP says no customer data was accessed and has replaced signing keys.

items.t: Hackers breach US Air Force 'Cloud One' platform
items.d: Intruders penetrated the Air Force's flagship cloud computing system, raising questions over military cloud security.

items.t: Nvidia pauses server shipments to Southeast Asia
items.d: Partners were told to halt shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia with no restart date, amid US checks on chips reaching China.

items.t: Belgium orders Google to halt data centre build
items.d: Authorities said Google made changes not covered by its permit, a rare block on AI-era data centre expansion in Europe.

items.t: New kidney-cancer drug shows promise in first human trial
items.d: In a Dana-Farber trial of the HIF-2 inhibitor imdatifan, 22% of patients with advanced kidney cancer saw their tumours shrink.

items.t: Africa's coastal cities are sinking, raising flood risk
items.d: Land subsidence could put over 7 million people and a million buildings at flood risk by 2050, a Science Advances study finds.

items.t: NIH studies link glyphosate weedkiller to cancer
items.d: Three studies by US government scientists contradict a recent EPA conclusion that the widely used herbicide is safe.

items.t: Energy bills expected to jump 26% in January
items.d: A gas price surge linked to the Iran war is set to push up the price cap sharply, squeezing households this winter.

items.t: Dozens of court cases hit by undisclosed AI use
items.d: At least 25 cases in England and Wales this year involved AI-generated material that wasn't declared, including fake citations.

items.t: Man United extend Bruno Fernandes to 2028
items.d: United activated an option keeping their captain at Old Trafford until summer 2028.

items.t: 歐盟峰會未能就預算及450億歐元烏克蘭貸款達成協議
items.d: 歐盟領袖未能就2028至34年度預算達成共識，捷克、匈牙利及斯洛伐克反對烏克蘭貸款。會談將於12月17至18日再開。

items.t: 烏克蘭提議黑海停火以保障糧食出口
items.d: 基輔提交黑海停火方案，正等待莫斯科回覆；此前據報俄羅斯在敖德薩附近襲擊兩艘外國運糧船。

items.t: 中東衝突威脅供應　油價徘徊數月高位
items.d: 有報道指荷姆茲海峽一帶發生油輪事故及發現水雷，布蘭特期油徘徊每桶約96美元，令人憂慮燃料及能源開支進一步上升。

items.t: 西班牙周日大選　各黨作最後拉票
items.d: 首相桑切斯與對手在周日大選前作最後呼籲，生活成本是主要議題。

items.t: 新西蘭執政聯盟差一席過半
items.d: 正式結果顯示執政聯盟取得130席中的65席，需與小黨商討才能執政。

items.t: 加拿大最高法院維持魁北克宗教標誌禁令
items.d: 最高法院以6比1裁決，大致維持禁止部分公職人員佩戴宗教標誌的「第21號法案」。

items.t: 華爾街反彈　納指升逾2%
items.d: 美股在AI股波動的一周大幅反彈，十年期美債孳息則升至約4.94%。

items.t: 挪威廉航Norse Atlantic因燃油成本申請破產
items.d: 這家挪威跨大西洋廉價航空公司歸咎航空燃油價格飆升，反映能源衝擊正打擊旅遊業。

items.t: 研究質疑Amazon黑色星期五「優惠」
items.d: 有分析發現約三分之二減價貨品早前售價相同甚至更低，Amazon對結果提出異議。

items.t: SAP考慮裁員逾萬人推動AI重組
items.d: 據報歐洲最大軟件公司正考慮大規模裁員，以配合AI重組。

items.t: OpenAI反告Apple盜取商業秘密及施壓供應商
items.d: OpenAI指Apple向共同供應商施壓、不與其合作，並盜用硬件設計，令Apple七月提出的訴訟進一步升級。

items.t: SAP證實遭網絡攻擊　據報源代碼受影響
items.d: 據報黑客以盜取的員工憑證複製及修改GitHub上的代碼。SAP指沒有客戶資料外洩，並已更換簽署密鑰。

items.t: 黑客入侵美國空軍「Cloud One」雲端平台
items.d: 黑客攻入美國空軍旗艦雲端運算系統，引發對軍方雲端保安的質疑。

items.t: Nvidia暫停向東南亞付運伺服器
items.d: Nvidia通知夥伴暫停向馬來西亞、新加坡、泰國及印尼付運，未定恢復日期，美國正加強追查晶片流入中國。

items.t: 比利時下令Google停建數據中心
items.d: 當局指Google作出許可證未涵蓋的改動，屬歐洲罕見阻止AI時代數據中心擴建的個案。

items.t: 新腎癌藥首次人體試驗見成效
items.d: 美國Dana-Farber癌症研究所測試HIF-2抑制劑imdatifan，22%晚期腎癌病人腫瘤縮小。

items.t: 非洲沿岸城市下沉　水浸風險增
items.d: 《Science Advances》研究指，地面下沉或令2050年前逾700萬人及100萬座建築物面臨水浸風險。

items.t: 美國國家衛生研究院研究指草甘膦與癌症有關
items.d: 三項美國政府科學家的研究，與環保局最近指這種常用除草劑安全的結論相矛盾。

items.t: 能源賬單料一月急升26%
items.d: 與伊朗戰爭有關的天然氣價格急升，料令能源價格上限大幅上調，今個冬天家庭負擔加重。

items.t: 數十宗法庭案件涉未披露使用AI
items.d: 今年英格蘭及威爾斯最少25宗案件涉及未申報的AI生成內容，包括虛構的案例引述。

items.t: 曼聯為「B費」續約至2028年
items.d: 曼聯啟動續約條款，留住隊長B費至2028年夏天。
